subject: Community/private-actor de facto management functions, AC reliance, Community debt and definitive-text compliance in Concurso 36/2012
verified_findings: Private actors performed stable functions over Community debt, voting, access, security and maintenance.
The Insolvency Administrator requested security, attended Community meetings, authorised identified access/maintenance acts and used creditor-generated debt material in court.
The 20 January 2017 Article 97 bis order formally made the Community pre-insolvency claim ordinary contingent without own amount.
The 8 February 2018 Article 97 bis order changed the credit holder to CAM without enlarging recognised quantum.
Later Community amounts were openly filed and used as liquidation or better-bid conditions; they are not currently identified as express definitive-text amendments.

No post-liquidation incident has yet been located that finally re-quantifies the Community claim, enlarges the EUR 9,052,251.69 privileged total or reclassifies every later interest component as definitive concursal credit.
central_hypothesis: Documented private performance of important management functions, combined with documented AC delegation/reliance and a creditor-generated debt architecture, supports a serious de facto-administration and knowing-facilitation investigation.
not_established: full administrator-in-fact status for all actors or functions
documentary falsity with knowledge and intent
AC delegation of hotel operation as such

direct_incident_answer.qualification: Complete certified court docket remains outstanding; not yet located is not proof of non-existence.
